# CollectionError

Why a collection operation could not be completed.

```rux
pub enum CollectionError: uint8 {
    OutOfMemory = 1,
    CapacityOverflow = 2,
    IndexOutOfRange = 3,
    Unsupported = 4
}
```

Every case means the operation did not happen and the collection is as it was.

## Cases

| Name               | Value | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `OutOfMemory`      | `1`   | The allocator had no storage to give. Transient in principle: the same request may succeed later, and a caller with something to release may make it so.                                                                                                                                        |
| `CapacityOverflow` | `2`   | The size the operation needed could not be represented. A count times an element size that does not fit in a `uint`, or a length plus a growth that wraps. Not a shortage of memory but of arithmetic: no allocator could have served the request, because the number naming it does not exist. |
| `IndexOutOfRange`  | `3`   | The index was not one the collection has.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `Unsupported`      | `4`   | The allocator refused the layout itself rather than running short. An alignment stricter than the allocator serves, or a block it did not hand out. Retrying is pointless: the same request will be refused the same way.                                                                       |

## Methods

<h3 id="is-transient"><code>IsTransient</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsTransient(self: CollectionError) -> bool
```

Whether the same operation might succeed later.
`self` is borrowed. True only for `OutOfMemory`, which says the allocator had nothing to give rather than
that the request was impossible. A capacity that cannot be represented will not start being representable,
an index the collection does not have will not appear, and a layout the allocator refuses will be refused
again.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: whether trying again could succeed

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/CollectionError.rux#L43)

## Implements Display

`CollectionError` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(
    self: &CollectionError,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the description of why an operation did not happen, or `no error` for success.
The five cases stay distinguishable in words as they are in the type: a shortage of memory is not a size that
cannot be named, and neither is a layout the allocator refuses outright. Those distinctions decide whether a
caller retries, so a description that blurred them would send somebody to fix the wrong thing.
The descriptions are stable. They are not a parsing contract: a program branches on the case.
Reports whatever the writer reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for any style or precision.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole description was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/CollectionError.rux#L255)

## Related

<h3 id="from-alloc-error"><code>FromAllocError</code></h3>

```rux
pub func FromAllocError(error: AllocError) -> CollectionError
```

The collection error that corresponds to an allocator's.
`error` is read by value. `OutOfMemory` stays itself, and `Unsupported` and `InvalidBlock`
both become `Unsupported`, because from a collection's side they are the same thing — the allocator will not
serve this, and asking again will not change that.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/CollectionError.rux#L56)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type         | Description               |
| ------- | ------------ | ------------------------- |
| `error` | `AllocError` | why the allocator refused |

**Returns**: the same failure as a collection error
